ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act, Act No. 17905 as amended; Commercial Registration Act, Act No. 16852 as amended; Act on Reporting and Using Specific Financial Transaction Information, Act No. 18968, Articles 2 and 5-2, and Presidential Enforcement Decree Article 11; Act on Prevention of Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction, Act No. 14475; Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Act No. 19067; Medical Devices Act, Act No. 18650; all administered in coordination with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU), National Tax Service, Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), and Supreme Court Registration Offices.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or registrar of companies in the country of the foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a competent notary public in the country of origin; for Hague Apostille Convention member states, affix Apostille only through the designated competent authority; for non-member states, follow notarization, authentication by the originating Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Consular Legalization by the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and Consular Legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive; they are never sequenced together.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Existence or Equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or other statutory registrar in the jurisdiction of the foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed solely by Hague Apostille for member states, or solely by Consular Legalization for non-member states; no mixed or chained authentication.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution Authorizing Formation of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or notary public, executed under the foreign parent's corporate governance rules
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified board resolution; for use in Korea, notarize the signature of the chair or secretary and then authenticate exclusively by Apostille (member state) or exclusively by Consular Legalization (non-member state).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent registry in the foreign parent's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy; Apostille is the exclusive path for member states; Consular Legalization is the exclusive path for non-member states; both paths are not to be combined.

Original bank letter on bank letterhead with authorized signature; must be notarized and then authenticated exclusively by Hague Apostille or exclusively by Consular Legalization depending on the issuing bank's jurisdiction.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal representative or director of the foreign parent before a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized UBO declaration; Korea-bound use must be authenticated exclusively via Apostille for member states and exclusively via Consular Legalization for non-member states.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, every direct and indirect shareholder, director, officer, ultimate beneficial owner, and authorized signatory must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions lists including DPRK-related Resolution 1718, EU and UK HM Treasury consolidated sanctions lists, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit administrative sanctions database, domestic Korean criminal and tax enforcement records, World Bank exclusion lists, and adverse-media sources. PEPs are defined under FATF standards to include current and former foreign and domestic prominent public officials, their family members, and close associates. All PEP relationships require enhanced due diligence, documented source of wealth, source of funds, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring before any corporate registration or bank account activation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Registration Information Center (i-REG, www.iros.go.kr) and the name-search facilities of the District Court Registration Offices; supplementary National Tax Service business registration portal for tax name clearance.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean commercial registry names must be written in Hangul. Foreign names used by the LLC must be phonetically transliterated into Hangul and may be accompanied by an English trade name for export and international banking purposes. The four-tier naming formula is: Unique Identification Element plus Business Purpose Element plus Company Form Element plus the legal suffix Yuhan Hoesa. The name must be distinguishable from all existing registered marks and must avoid misleading industry or government connotations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the proposed name is rejected, incorporating counsel must file a written objection with the registration judge of the competent District Court within fourteen days of rejection, citing the legal basis for availability, submitting three alternative Hangul variants, and paying the prescribed appeal fee. The registration judge must issue a written decision within one month. If the objection is again denied, the applicant may institute administrative litigation before the relevant Administrative Court pursuant to the Administrative Litigation Act, and may request suspensive relief against any provisional refusal. During the appeal period, no parallel filing may be made under a confusingly similar name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For an IVD manufacturing LLC under ISIC 3250 and NAICS 334516, virtual office, commercial mailbox, or serviced-address-only arrangements are not acceptable. The National Tax Service, local municipal tax authorities, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS), and commercial banks will reject the entity for medical device registration, VAT registration, and account opening unless the registered office is a physical leased or owned workspace sufficient for microfluidic cartridge manufacturing, immunoassay analyzer inventory, quality control, and regulatory inspection. A serviced office may be used only for ancillary administrative functions, never as the sole registered commercial substance. Banks additionally require an executed lease certificate in the company's name and recent utility invoices and may conduct their own on-site visit.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist includes: registered office must match the actual production site; company signboard must be visibly installed; lease certificate, utility bills, employee payroll records, equipment inventory, quality-control records, and supply-chain documentation must be present. Quantified risk: High, approximately 75% to 85% probability of an announced or unannounced inspection within the first twelve months because MFDS coordinates pre-licensure inspections for IVD manufacturing, municipal tax offices verify commercial substance, and banks conduct physical verification before activating payment rails such as Swift_LC and TT_Wire.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended through 2023), Articles 287-2 through 287-60 (Yuhan Hoesa / Limited Liability Company), Articles 34, 35, 36, 39 and 42 relating to corporate registration, corporate name and registered office; Medical Devices Act (Act No. 13865, as amended) Articles 6, 14 and 15 for medical device manufacturing licensing; Foreign Investment Promotion Act for non-resident equity participation where applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Division, Local District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office of Yuhan Hoesa in the Republic of Korea, with the electronic submission portal operated by the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO); KOTRA Investment Support Center may be used as the single window for foreign-invested entities.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Commercial Registration of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa) together with the Articles of Incorporation (Jeonggwan), filed with the Commercial Registration Division of the Local District Court under Article 287-4 and Article 42 of the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act imposes no statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa. However, the total initial capital subscribed by the founding members must be actually contributed in cash or in kind before the commercial registration is completed, must be identified in the Articles of Incorporation, and must be deposited in a domestic bank account in the name of the company or for the account of the company during formation. For non-resident members, if the aggregate foreign investment is at least KRW 100 million, advance or post-closing notice to KOTRA under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act may be required, and banks may require source-of-funds documentation for the blocked or provisional deposit.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING MEMBERS ACTING AS THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA (THE COMPANY), ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN ACCORDANCE WITH ARTICLES 287-2 THROUGH 287-60 OF THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA AND THE COMPANY'S ARTICLES OF INCORPORATION. WHEREAS, the Company is being organized as a limited liability company (Yuhan Hoesa) in the Republic of Korea for the manufacture of microfluidic cartridges and automated point-of-care immunoassay in vitro diagnostic analyzers under ISIC 3250; and WHEREAS, the founding members have fully subscribed to the total initial capital contributions set forth in the Articles of Incorporation; and WHEREAS, it is necessary to adopt initial corporate governance, banking arrangements, registered office, and statutory officers before the commercial registration filing. NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED: (1) SHARE CAPITAL AND SUBSCRIPTION: The total initial capital contributions of the Company, as stated in the Articles of Incorporation, are hereby approved, and each founding member's subscription is accepted in full. The Representative Member and Chief Financial Officer are directed to deposit all subscribed capital into a corporate account maintained with a bank licensed in the Republic of Korea and to hold those funds for the exclusive use of the Company pending completion of commercial registration. (2) BANKING AUTHORIZATION: The Company shall open domestic and foreign-currency operating accounts at a Korean bank. The Representative Member, the Chief Financial Officer, and any two officers named in a separate officer list are jointly and severally authorized to execute banking applications, signature cards, internet banking agreements, foreign-exchange declarations, treasury payment instructions, and bank proof-of-capital certificates. (3) REGISTERED OFFICE: The registered office of the Company shall be at the address identified in the Articles of Incorporation, within the jurisdiction of the Local District Court where registration is sought. The corporate seal, member register, statutory records, financial books, and audit files shall be maintained at that address, and all service of process, tax summonses, and official notices may be delivered there. (4) APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS: The following officers are appointed effective as of the date of this Resolution: (a) the Representative Member/Chief Executive Officer, with full authority to manage the business, represent the Company in dealings with the District Court, National Tax Service, MFDS, banks, and any public authority, and to execute all documents required to effect the incorporation; (b) the Chief Financial Officer, with authority over tax filings, accounting, treasury, and bank relationships; (c) the Technical Qualified Person for Medical Device Manufacturing, holding qualifications acceptable to the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety under the Medical Devices Act, responsible for the quality management system, GMP compliance, IVD product release, labeling, adverse-event vigilance, and regulatory file maintenance; and (d) the Corporate Auditor, if required by law or the Articles of Incorporation, to inspect financial and management matters and report to the members. (5) EXECUTION AND FILING: The Representative Member and any one other officer are authorized to execute and submit the Application for Commercial Registration, to request issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation Registration, and thereafter to apply for business registration, medical device manufacturing licenses, environmental approvals, and fire safety certificates. (6) OMNIBUS AUTHORIZATION: External counsel, certified tax accountants, licensed notaries public, GMP consultants, and regulatory agents may be retained to implement this Resolution. This Resolution is final, valid, and binding on the Company and its members and may be presented to banks, notaries, courts, tax authorities, and licensing agencies as conclusive evidence of corporate action.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Pre-Filing Review with the Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO) and the Commercial Registration Division of the Local District Court having jurisdiction over the proposed registered office in Korea.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage Korean incorporation counsel or access the IRO portal to conduct a corporate-name search. The selected name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an already registered Korean company in the same registry. The search should cover the Korean company name and any English trade-name translation. If the name is available, prepare the draft Articles of Incorporation containing the exact legal name, business objects, ISIC 3250 scope, total initial capital, contribution units, registered office address, officer provisions, fiscal year, and dissolution rules. Submit the proposed name and corporate structure for a preliminary court review if the registry office offers a pre-examination service; if the review is unavailable, proceed to step 2. All documents must be in Korean or accompanied by a certified Korean translation for later filing.
required_dossiers: Corporate name search request and IRO search result receipt
Passport or alien registration cards of all founding members
Power of attorney naming the Korean incorporation agent
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean
Beneficial ownership and ultimate beneficial owner statement
Proposed registered office address and lease or letter of intent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or for public-policy grounds, select two alternative names and immediately re-file the search request. If the IRO portal suspends the application because of incomplete document authentication, ask the registry officer to provide a written deficiency note, correct the documents, and re-submit at the same court counter or through the online correction function; no additional court fee is charged for a mere name substitution if the filing has not yet been accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of the Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed notary public under the Notary Public Act of the Republic of Korea; for overseas members, the Korean consulate or embassy may attest signatures after apostille or consular legalization.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Polish the Articles of Incorporation to reflect Korean limited-liability-company statutory content, including total capital, number and value of contribution units, contribution method, object clause, registered office, appointment mechanism of officers, transfer restriction rules, duration, annual meeting requirements, and liquidation clause. The founders must execute the Articles; Korean law practice typically requires notarization to satisfy banks and the court registry. The notary will confirm the identity and legal capacity of every founder, verify the document contains no unlawful object, and certify the signatures. After notarization, no substantive change may be made without repeating the certification. Provide a Korean translation of foreign-issued identity documents and ensure corporate officers initial every page if required by the notary.
required_dossiers: Final Korean language Articles of Incorporation
Notarized or apostilled identity documents of founders
Certificate of personal seal impression of each founder
Draft board resolution approving the Articles
Power of attorney for notarization
Proof of address and registered office plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses certification because of an unlawful object or ambiguous capital clause, correct the Articles and resubmit. If the notary raises a signature discrepancy, provide fresh signature specimen or a new power of attorney. A court notary or another notary may be substituted; in extreme cases, file an application with the District Court under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure to seek an order compelling the notary to certify the lawful document.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Initial Capital and Opening of the Corporate Formation Banking Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean commercial banking institution licensed by the Financial Services Commission; for foreign investment reporting, KOTRA or the designated foreign-exchange bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional corporate formation account in the name of the Yuhan Hoesa company or in the names of the founders jointly in trust for the Company. Transfer the full subscribed capital into that account in KRW or convertible foreign currency. Obtain from the bank a certificate of deposit of paid-in capital, stating the account holder, total amount, date of deposit, and confirmation that the deposited funds are unavailable for withdrawal except upon presentation of the Certificate of Incorporation Registration or a written order of the court. If any founder is a non-resident and the investment equals or exceeds KRW 100 million, file the advance foreign investment notice with KOTRA or the bank before transfer, and keep the issued certificate of foreign investment report for submission to the court and tax office. If capital is paid in kind, obtain an appraised report by a licensed appraiser describing the contributed assets.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank account application for formation account
Passport or foreign residency card of each subscriber
Source of funds declaration and recent bank statements
Certificate of foreign investment report or FDI notice receipt, if applicable
Appraisal report for in-kind contributions, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines to open the account due to anti-money-laundering concerns, submit a beneficial ownership form, explain the source of funds with transaction receipts, and escalate to the bank's compliance officer or the foreign-investment desk. If the bank still refuses after five business days, approach another licensed bank recommended by KOTRA and request a written refusal note from the first bank to expedite the alternative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration Filing with the Local District Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Division of the Local District Court with exclusive territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; electronic filing through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Application for Commercial Registration of Yuhan Hoesa together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, bank certificate of paid-in capital, written consents of the appointed officers, specimen signatures, certificate of personal seal impression, and the foreign investment certificate if applicable. Verify that the business object expressly states the manufacture of medical devices, microfluidic cartridges, and in-vitro diagnostic analyzers. Pay the court registration fee, local education surtax, and certificate fee at the court window or via electronic tax transfer. The court registrar will examine statutory formalities, record the Company in the commercial register, and issue the Certificate of Incorporation Registration, which generally contains the company registration number, name, capital, and registered office. After issuance, the officers must not operate under the corporate name until the applicant receives the certified copy.
required_dossiers: Commercial registration application form for a Yuhan Hoesa
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of paid-in capital deposit issued by the bank
Written appointment consents from all initial officers
Seal impression certificate of the corporate representative
Certificate of foreign investment report, if applicable
Power of attorney filed by the Korean agent
Application for certificate of incorporation registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a deficiency notice, cure each cited item within the statutory supplementary period, usually two weeks, by uploading the corrected form via IRO or appearing with original documents. If the court suspends registration because the business object is too broad or the name is confusingly similar, amend the Articles, re-notarize, and pay the supplementary fee. If registration is refused, file a petition for immediate appeal to the High Court under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure within two weeks or file an administrative appeal to the competent court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with the National Tax Service and Post-Incorporation Tax Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office of the National Tax Service having jurisdiction over the registered office of Yuhan Hoesa.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of receiving the Certificate of Incorporation Registration, apply for business registration under the Framework Act on National Taxes. Submit the corporate registration certificate, adoption of the corporate seal certificate, registered office lease agreement, representative's identification, and proof of bank account opening. The tax office issues a Business Registration Certificate with a unique corporate tax identification number. Use this certificate to open the permanent operating bank account, register the company for value-added tax, file the corporate tax pre-registration, and register with the local municipal authorities for property and local consumption taxes. The company must also register its actual workplace and manufacturing facility with the relevant local government for job creation and industrial support programs.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation Registration
Business registration application form (NTS Form)
Corporate seal impression certificate
Registered office lease contract or ownership proof
Identification of representative member
Bank account proof or certificate of bank appointment
Power of attorney for the tax accountant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office rejects or delays the business registration due to missing lease proof or unresolved office verification, file a written correction with the supporting lease security deposit agreement and floor plan. If the district tax office fails to issue the certificate within five business days, request expedited issuance from the tax office complaint coordinator or file a tax administrative petition under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Medical Device Manufacturing License, Environmental Registration, and Fire Safety Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) Medical Device Safety Bureau; local municipal environmental agency delegated by the Ministry of Environment; National Fire Agency and local fire safety authority.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration of the Yuhan Hoesa, submit to MFDS an application for a Medical Device Manufacturing License covering the manufacture of microfluidic cartridges and automated point-of-care immunoassay analyzers. Prepare a quality management system file aligned with ISO 13485 and Korean Good Manufacturing Practice requirements for in-vitro diagnostic products. MFDS will review the manufacturing facility layout, cleanroom HVAC verifications, water systems, equipment qualification, personnel qualifications, and quality-control procedures for the IVD analyzer and cartridge. Simultaneously, file an environmental registration or preliminary environmental review with the local environmental agency; the classification depends on total floor area, wastewater discharge volume, and hazardous chemical use. Obtain from the local fire authority the Fire Safety Completion Inspection Certificate after installation of fire suppression systems, and file an industrial workplace safety checklist with the Ministry of Employment and Labor if manufacturing operations create physical, chemical, or biological hazards.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation Registration
Business Registration Certificate
Medical Device Manufacturing License application form
Manufacturing facility floor plan, cleanroom design, and utility drawings
GMP quality manual, SOPs, validation protocols, and equipment calibration records
Technical files for the IVD analyzer and microfluidic cartridge
Environmental registration form or small-scale environmental impact assessment report
Wastewater and VOC emission calculations and proposed treatment system
Hazardous chemical inventory and safety data sheets
Fire safety completion certificate and civil-defense fire inspection report
MSDS register and workplace safety risk assessment under the Occupational Safety and Health Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MFDS or the local authority issues a deficiency letter, respond with the requested technical, environmental, or fire-safety documentation within the stated cure period. If the manufacturing license is refused, request a written refusal statement and file an administrative appeal with the Central Administrative Appeals Commission within 30 days, or supplement the GMP file through MFDS pre-consultation and resubmit after making the required facility corrections.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) Medical Device Safety Bureau; Ministry of Environment through the local environmental agency; National Fire Agency and the relevant local fire safety inspection office; Ministry of Employment and Labor for occupational safety and health clearance.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing License and Medical Device GMP Certification for In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices issued under the Medical Devices Act of the Republic of Korea, together with the Fire Safety Completion Inspection Certificate, Environmental Discharge Registration or Small-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment approval, and Chemical Accident Prevention Plan approval if threshold quantities of hazardous substances are stored or used.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Republic of Korea, through the local environmental administration office or Korea Environment Corporation for delegated environmental review and wastewater/emission approvals.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C-Environmental Registration and Preliminary Environmental Review for a typical below-threshold IVD manufacturing plant beneath the small-scale assessment floor-area thresholds; Category B-Small-Scale Environmental Impact Assessment where the total building floor area is at least 5,000 square meters or the project site is located in an environmentally sensitive or mountainous zone; a full Environmental Impact Assessment Report is required only if the project involves a total site area of at least 150,000 square meters or is otherwise designated as a high-impact project under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act. The applicant must obtain a written tier confirmation from the local environmental agency before the factory construction is approved.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Process wastewater from IVD and microfluidic cartridge manufacturing must meet Korean national effluent standards: pH 6.5-8.5, BOD no greater than 10 mg/L, COD no greater than 20 mg/L, suspended solids no greater than 10 mg/L, total nitrogen no greater than 20 mg/L, total phosphorus no greater than 0.4 mg/L, and no detectable oil film, or stricter local water-source protection limits where the local ordinance so requires. Cleanroom HVAC VOC emissions must satisfy the Clean Air Conservation Act facility-emission concentration limits and odor standards under the Malodor Prevention Act, including ammonia at no more than 1 ppm, hydrogen sulfide at no more than 0.02 ppm, and mercaptan compounds at no more than 0.002 ppm at the boundary line; hazardous chemical storage above the threshold quantities requires a Chemical Accident Prevention Plan and compliance with chemical substance release-reporting obligations. Biological IVD waste, used cartridges, clinical specimen residues, and inactivated microbial media must be autoclaved or otherwise rendered non-infectious and then transported by a licensed medical waste disposal operator in conformity with the Medical Waste Management Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The factory must obtain the Fire Safety Completion Inspection Certificate under the Fire Prevention and Safety Supervision Act, which requires automatic fire extinguishing systems, fire alarm systems, emergency evacuation lighting, fire-resistant structural materials, and Civil Defense facility compliance where the local government designates the area as a disaster-preparedness zone. The building must obtain a final building usage approval and conditional factory establishment approval from the local municipal authority. Under the Occupational Safety and Health Act, the company must submit a workplace safety and health risk assessment, provide personal protective equipment for chemical handling and laboratory operations, register high-risk chemical related facilities, implement an emergency response plan, display material safety data sheets, and, if the site stores or processes hazardous chemicals above the applicable threshold quantity, submit a Process Safety Management plan to the Ministry of Employment and Labor. Any cleanroom or biohazard area must be commissioned and validated before MFDS GMP inspection, and the fire authority must re-inspect after any significant modification of the manufacturing line.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; primary online portal HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr) for corporate tax, VAT, business registration, and e-tax invoices; Korea Customs Service (UNI-PASS) for export clearance and customs declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity, the Korean Tax Identification Number is the 10-digit Business Registration Number issued by the district tax office. The Yuhan Hoesa (LLC) must appoint a domestic place of business or a Korean tax agent, file the business registration application through HomeTax or in person at the competent district tax office within 20 days of commencement of business, and submit the entity formation articles, proof of foreign registration, ownership and director identification, power of attorney, and lease or proof of the Korean place of business. If no Korean place of business is established, a non-resident supplier that makes taxable supplies may still obtain VAT registration through a tax representative using the simplified non-resident registration procedure under the Value-Added Tax Act; the NTS then issues a 10-digit registered tax invoice number (BRN/VAT ID).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None under Korean tax law. Korea does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election. A foreign-invested Yuhan Hoesa with a Korean domestic place of business is taxed at entity level as a domestic corporation; it may elect a non-calendar fiscal year for corporate tax purposes with NTS approval, but no pass-through election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Republic of Korea Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration turnover threshold; every person commencing a business in Korea must register with the competent district tax office from the date of business commencement. The simplified taxable person status with a lower VAT calculation burden is limited to small natural persons with annual revenue below the statutory limit and is not available to a Yuhan Hoesa LLC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All B2B tax invoices must be issued electronically through the NTS HomeTax e-tax invoice system and transmitted to the NTS by no later than the day after the supply date. Korea does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or anti-fraud digital stamping model; instead, the NTS cross-matches e-tax invoices, credit card sales data, and cash receipt records. Foreign suppliers registered domestically must also issue e-tax invoices when making domestic taxable supplies. Failure to issue or transmit e-tax invoices triggers penalties based on the supply value.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to tangible goods exported from Korea when title and risk pass to a foreign buyer, the goods are physically shipped from Korea, and the exporter retains the official export declaration from Korea Customs Service. Qualifying offshore services and services directly related to exported goods may also be zero-rated where the benefit and use occur outside Korea. For the IVD microfluidic cartridges and immunoassay analyzers, the exporter must prove the foreign destination, actual customs clearance, and receipt of foreign currency proceeds from the export sale.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (Electronic Customs Clearance Number / Bill of Entry)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export shipment
Commercial invoice including product description, HS code, quantity, and foreign sale price
Packing list for the exported IVD consignment
Foreign Exchange Transaction Confirmation or Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the foreign buyer
Certificate of Origin or other destination-customs documentation if required by the importing country
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If export documents are invalid, incomplete, or fraudulent, the NTS and Korea Customs Service will deny the 0% rate, reassess VAT at 10%, and impose additional tax penalties of up to 40% of the understated tax for dishonest returns. False invoices and fraudulent export refunds may trigger criminal tax evasion penalties, fines, imprisonment, and retrospective clawback of refunded amounts with statutory interest. Export proceeds not repatriated within the statutory 180-day period may also be treated as unreported income and result in both corporate income tax and VAT exposure, plus foreign exchange and trade regulation penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK); with policy authority jointly administered by the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a mostly liberalized current account convertibility regime. Import and export payments, service fees, royalties, and other commercial settlements are freely convertible through authorized foreign exchange banks provided the underlying transaction is documented and reported through the Foreign Exchange Information System. Capital account transactions, including inbound foreign direct investment, intercompany loans, and cross-border financing, require notification or registration with the Ministry of Economy and Finance or the Bank of Korea depending on the instrument. Korean residents are obliged to report foreign currency receipts and disbursements to the authorized bank; the bank transmits the declaration to the authorities. Corporate profit remittances, such as dividends and liquidation proceeds for registered foreign investment, are generally permitted subject to actual dividend evidence, corporate income tax clearance, and the foreign investment registration certificate. The principal practical hurdle for treasury operations is the limited offshore accessibility of Korean won. Because won is not fully convertible in offshore markets, most cross-border trade and capital flows are settled in major delivery currencies, typically US dollars. Non-resident entities must also ensure their beneficial ownership declarations are consistent with the bank's Anti-Money Laundering file, as Korean regulators require the ultimate beneficial owner to be disclosed and current. There is no blanket surrender rule requiring converters to sell all export proceeds into won; exporters may hold their proceeds in foreign exchange accounts, but the original export claim must be collected within the statutory window and reported. Overall, current account flows face moderate friction; capital flows face moderate to high documentary friction but are legally transactable when fully registered.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must physically be received to a foreign exchange bank in Korea or into a Korean exporter's certified foreign currency account within six months from the date of the export declaration, unless an extension period has been approved by the designated foreign exchange bank. There is no compulsory conversion ratio into Korean won; the exporter may retain the proceeds in a foreign currency account or convert them as needed. The collection and arrival of proceeds must be reported to the foreign exchange bank and through the electronic Foreign Exchange Information System to satisfy the export settlement requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Investment Registered Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Import-Export Trade Settlement Foreign Currency Account
Foreign Investment Capital Account / Basic Operational KRW and Foreign Currency Account
Corporate Operational Currency Account / Trade Services Foreign Currency Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low - Materially Non-Viable. Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions have no direct regulatory license under Korea's Electronic Financial Transactions Act. They are not authorized to hold Korean won deposits, issue Korean won settlement accounts, or provide local payment and current account services to a Korean-domesticated legal entity. A foreign EMI may only enter through licensing or an approved partnership with an authorized Korean commercial bank, and even then the actual clearing must sit with the domestic bank. For this IVD manufacturing operation, the safe route is to use a licensed tier-one domestic bank as the primary treasury and clearing house; the EMI is not a compliant standalone clearing alternative.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory directors, authorized signatories, and the ultimate beneficial owners must appear physically in a Korean bank branch for identity verification and signature specimen confirmation. Remote and consular proxy arrangements are generally not accepted on a standalone basis; a Korean embassy consular notarization may be used as supplementary identity evidence only if the designated bank compliance committee grants a written waiver. For the foreign parent entity, board resolutions and legal entity documents must be apostilled or consular legalized, and the Korean named director or representative officer should present his or her passport, Alien Registration Card or corporate residence certification, and the corporate seal certificate. No account opening is permanently feasible without a face-to-face interview and satisfactory enhanced due diligence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership opacity caused by nominee shareholders or a multi-tier non-resident holding structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled legalized certificate of incorporation; latest registered shareholder register; consolidated group beneficial ownership chart to the first natural person; beneficial ownership declaration forms under Korean AML rules; passport copies and address proof for each natural-person shareholder; board resolution explaining the commercial purpose of the Korean Yuhan Hoesa and the roles of local directors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade and manufacturing invoice mismatch where the import of microfluidic cartridges or IVD analyzer inputs does not align with goods description, HS codes, and price benchmarks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original purchase orders; supplier commercial invoices; Korean Logistics/UNI-PASS customs declarations; packing lists; bill of lading and airway bill; HS classification memorandum; technical product specification sheets supporting the component prices; documentary evidence that the bank's trade and FX purpose codes reflect the true nature of the transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Routing of funds through unlicensed money transmitters, shell correspondents, or any cryptocurrency or virtual-asset settlement channel.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SWIFT MT199/MT103 message trails and correspondent bank advisories; proof that all originating and beneficiary accounts are held at licensed financial institutions; signed compliance attestation that no cryptocurrency or unlicensed payment instrument has been used in commercial settlement; screening outputs against sanctions lists and adverse media; CFO undertaking that invoice payments will only be executed from a named Korean corporate bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Export controls and medical-device dual-use suspicion arising from IVD immunoassay analyzers with potential laboratory research applications.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Korea MFDS medical device manufacturing authorization and product registration; KOTRA/MOTIE foreign investment notification; export commodity classification and ECCN determination; end-user certificate and destination control statement for each buyer; technical file declaring the diagnostic purpose and absence of biological-agent manufacturing capability; customs clearance records proving legitimate entry and use.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection must follow the Foreign Investment Promotion Act. The foreign investor files a foreign investment declaration before or within two months after receiving the funds. The capital amount must be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the investor's own regulated bank account to the chosen tier-one Korean bank. The purpose of payment should be stated as Foreign Direct Investment, capital contribution, or paid-in capital increase, using the Korean foreign exchange transaction purpose code that matches equity investment. After the bank confirms receipt, the investor obtains a certificate of foreign investment registration and the entity completes capital verification by engaging a Korean certified public accountant. The verified capital must remain in the designated foreign investment escrow account and cannot be released for operational expenses until registration is completed.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements will clear primarily through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers, Commercial Letters of Credit opened at the Korean bank under MT700 instructions, and documentary collections under the Uniform Rules for Collections. For high-value IVD analyzer shipments, a confirmed commercial LC provides settlement certainty. For repetitive OEM component purchases, SWIFT MT103 transfers against matched invoices and packing documents are acceptable. All outbound payments require a valid tax invoice, customs export declaration, foreign exchange purpose code, and the operational contract or purchase order proving the underlying trade. No settlement via fintech EMI prepaid accounts or virtual-asset platforms is permitted.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Korean won/US dollar forward contracts offered by authorized Korean banks to hedge real trade receivables and payables; physical delivery required.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible only through onshore authorized banks on a restricted basis to hedge exposure arising from genuine cross-border trade finance transactions; speculative NDF positions are prohibited.

Cross-currency swaps are permissible solely for covered interest and principal exposures on registered foreign currency loans or capital-related exposures and must be supported by the underlying loan agreement and Board-approved treasury policy; leveraged or speculative rollovers are not acceptable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa, no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unfiled amounts attract a 20% negligence penalty plus 0.022% per day late-payment interest; continued non-payment permits NTS seizure of bank accounts, accounts receivable and property, and may support a court order for administrative dissolution of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government (Metropolitan City/Province or Si/Gun/Gu) via WeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the corporate income tax return deadline; for a calendar-year company, no later than 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Unpaid local income tax is subject to a 20% negligence penalty, 0.022% daily delay interest and local government collection measures including compulsory sale of assets.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 10 February of each year for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitted or incorrect withholding reconciliation attracts a 20% negligence penalty, 0.022% daily delay interest, and further sanctions for failure to issue withholding certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First-period preliminary return by 25 April, final first-half return by 25 July, second-period preliminary return by 25 October, final annual return by 25 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitted VAT liability attracts 10% or 20% negligence penalties depending on intention or registration failure, plus 0.022% daily delay interest; serious habitual non-filing may lead to business registration suspension or cancellation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements and External Auditor's Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through DART system, if the company is subject to external audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end for approval by the members' meeting; the audit report must be submitted to DART within 3 weeks after the members' approval meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or to file the audit report carries administrative fines of up to KRW 30 million (approximately USD 22,000); false reporting may trigger criminal penalties of up to 5 years' imprisonment or a fine of up to KRW 50 million.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records; minutes and resolutions must be maintained at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be convened within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, by 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the statutory meeting or to maintain the minute book exposes the company and responsible officers to a fine for non-compliant commercial registration of up to KRW 5 million and to a court-appointed inspector if any member petitions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory Register Audit and Annual Maintenance Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records made available to court-appointed inspectors, external auditors, and NTS on request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Immediately before the annual members' meeting, verified no later than 15 March for calendar-year companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-maintenance of the register of members, directors, charges, or minute book may result in court-imposed fines under the Commercial Act; failure to correct orders after judicial notice may ground administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Korean Court Registry (Commercial Registration), with simultaneous notification to NTS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 weeks after the date of transfer of a membership interest or any change in directors or representative
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration invites court administrative fines up to KRW 5 million under the Commercial Registration Act; an unregistered transfer may be unopposable to third parties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Medical Device Manufacturing Business License Maintenance and GMP Compliance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) and accredited medical device GMP audit body
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual compliance confirmation due before the manufacturing license anniversary date; MFDS renewal application should be filed at least 60 days before any item license expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operation without an effective MFDS manufacturing license or GMP certification can lead to administrative disposition, product sales ban, business closure order, and criminal fines under the Medical Devices Act; continued non-compliance may result in permanent license revocation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 15 February of the following calendar year if any non-resident member holds equity in the Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the annual foreign investment report may subject the foreign investor to a fine under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and may restrict the benefits attached to foreign-invested enterprise status.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and Others, as applied to a Yuhan Hoesa, an independent certified public accountant audit is mandatory when the company meets any of the following at the balance-sheet date: total assets of at least KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.0 million); annual turnover of at least KRW 100 billion (approximately USD 75.0 million); or an average of 300 or more full-time employees. Smaller LLCs are not statutorily required to appoint a CPA auditor unless external audit is required by the MFDS license, lender covenants, group audit policies, or a members' meeting resolution. In all audit-triggering cases, the auditor must be registered under the Act on External Audit and must issue an opinion on the financial statements before the statutory members' meeting deadline.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Mandatorily audited entities apply Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS); unlisted SMEs may elect Korean GAAP applicable to Small and Medium Enterprises (K-GAAP/SME) unless financial institutions or foreign counterparties require K-IFRS. All records must comply with the Korean Commercial Act and the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and Others.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: There is no generally applicable annual beneficial-ownership return for a Korean Yuhan Hoesa. Instead, the company must keep the statutory member register continuously current at the registered office and must file any shareholding or control transfer with the competent Korean court within 3 weeks (21 days) of the change. For AML/CFT purposes, the company and its financial service providers must identify and confirm the beneficial owner upon onboarding and on any material change; an internal annual UBO confirmation memorandum is recommended for the Medium_Risk_Enhanced IVD manufacturing profile. Foreign investors must also comply with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act reporting windows.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - USD 25,000 per annum for a compliant Korean GAAP/K-IFRS audit of an SME IVD manufacturer

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% top marginal national Corporate Income Tax ('CIT') rate for taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; progressive rates are 9% for the first KRW 200 million, 19% for KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% for KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 24% above KRW 300 billion, exclusive of the 10% local income tax surtax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No broad patent box regime exists; incentives are available through Korean Tax Incentives and Limitation Law, including R&D tax credits, temporary investment tax credits, foreign-investment tax incentives in designated free economic zones, and SME tax reduction under certain statutory thresholds; ordinary manufacturing LLCs outside designated zones may claim limited R&D and facility investment deductions but must meet contemporaneous documentation rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return for Tax Base and Tax Calculation (Form 1 / Corporation Tax Return) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; interim prepayments and quarterly estimated installment filings are required for medium and large corporate taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual CIT return must be filed within 3 months after the close of the fiscal year, i.e., by March 31 for a calendar year-end company; a further 3-month extension may be granted upon application, and separate interim semi-annual installment filings apply to certain large corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxpayer Identification and Fiscal Year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the entity's legal name, Korean business registration number, head office address, legal form 'Yuhan Hoesa (LLC)', fiscal year-end, incorporation date, and place of effective management.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean Taxpayer Reference Number exactly and disclose the non-resident ultimate beneficial owner and foreign shareholding percentage. The Korean LLC must show actual management and operational substance in Korea; an address that is merely a registered agent or letter-box will trigger anti-abuse review under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Law on Coordination of International Tax Affairs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Business Classification and Principal Industrial Activity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose ISIC Rev.4 code 3250, NAICS 2022 code 334516, and describe principal activity as manufacture of microfluidic cartridges, immunoassay analyzers, and in-vitro diagnostic medical devices.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The filing must clearly state 'Korean manufacturer and principal seller' rather than 'subject to foreign parent direction without local substance'. Cross-border wire transfers denominated in Swift/LC or T/T must be reconciled to the Korean entity's books; any mismatch between declared manufacturing activity and no physical facility, employees, or controlled raw-material inventory creates a transfer pricing red flag.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Financial Statements and Net Income per Korean GAAP/IFRS
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report revenue from cartridge sales, analyzer sales, spare parts, service and calibration agreements; cost of goods sold, gross profit, operating expenses, non-operating expenses, and book income before tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile IFRS book income to taxable income; make statutory add-backs for non-deductible entertainment, donations, penalties, and excessive management fees paid to overseas affiliates. Revenue recognized from export sales routed through a foreign group distribution hub must be supported by a distribution agreement, documented functions performed, and an arm's-length commission or resale-price analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Statutory Adjustments, Reserves, Depreciation and Temporary Differences
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter fiscal-period additions and deductions permitted under the Corporate Tax Act, including depreciation, bad debt reserves, accrued expenses, and timing differences between book income and taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders may not unilaterally shift head-office or shared-service expenses to the Korean LLC without a cost-contribution or service agreement, actual rendering of service, and benefit substantiation. Deductibility of intercompany royalties for IVD technology depends on license registration and economic use of IP in Korea; unsupported accruals to foreign affiliates are subject to add-back and withholding tax assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Foreign Related-Party Transactions and Transfer Pricing Adjustment Schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose each foreign related-party transaction category: sale of finished products, purchase of raw materials, intragroup service fees, royalty payments, interest on intercompany loans, and allocation of residual profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select an OECD-approved arm's-length method, attach a contemporaneous benchmarking study, and compute any transfer-pricing adjustment before entering taxable income. For point-of-care IVD distribution, a functional analysis must show which party owns product IP, inventory risk, warranty risk, and regulatory approval; an artificial systematic loss in Korea is the clearest trigger for a tax audit and re-determination under Article 6 of the Law on Coordination of International Tax Affairs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Taxable Income and Net Operating Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the final taxable base after deducting previously incurred losses, charitable contribution carryforwards, and other statutory deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses sustained by the Korean legal entity are deductible; losses of the foreign parent, group entities, or pre-incorporation expenses cannot be carried forward. NOL utilization must be separately scheduled by loss year and is available for 10 years; use of loss carryforwards to reduce taxable income while still paying high royalties to a related licensor will be questioned on both transfer-pricing and anti-avoidance grounds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Corporate Tax Computation Using Progressive Rate Brackets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the statutory rates of 9%, 19%, 21%, and 24% to the computed tax base and derive the national Corporate Income Tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean LLC is taxed at the entity level regardless of non-resident shareholding. Retained profits that are not distributed but remain in excess of working-capital needs may be treated as constructive dividend or deemed income disposition under Corporate Tax Act Article 67; therefore, a coherent dividend policy and economic-substance explanation should be documented in the Board minutes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Tax Credits, Foreign Tax Credits, Withholdings and Amount Payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter R&D credits, employment tax credits, foreign tax credits on foreign-source income, interim prepayments, and quarterly estimated payments; compute the balance of tax due or refund.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Korean LLC receives interest or royalties from foreign customers, the underlying foreign withholding tax can be claimed as a foreign tax credit subject to the Korean jurisdictional-source rules and treaty limitations. Non-resident shareholders cannot credit Korean taxes on their individual dividend receipt against the LLC's corporate tax; the LLC must, however, attach withholding certificates for outbound dividends paid during the year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the 10% local income tax surtax on the national Corporate Income Tax liability and report it separately on the combined HomeTax filing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Most Korean tax treaties extend coverage to national and local taxes, but the withholding agent must still verify the specific treaty wording. For non-resident shareholders claiming reduced withholding tax on dividends, both the national WHT and the local surtax must be reviewed; an erroneous claim of complete exemption without a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial-ownership statement will be penalized as under-withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 - Attachments and Non-Resident Treaty Disclosures
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attach audited financial statements, tax adjustment computation, transfer pricing Master File and Local File, foreign related-party transaction statement, DTA relief applications, Tax Residency Certificates, and beneficial-ownership declarations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any non-resident shareholder claiming treaty relief on Korean-sourced dividends, interest, or royalties must submit the completed withholding-tax reduction/exemption application together with a valid Tax Residency Certificate and a beneficial-ownership statement to the withholding agent before or on the date of payment. Missing attachments are treated as statutory non-compliance and lead to the unfiled-rate WHT assessment, interest surcharges, and possible criminal referral for abusive conduit arrangements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an additional 20% of the unpaid tax where no return is filed, 10% for an under-reported tax base, and 40% for fraudulent or sham under-reporting; a daily overdue surcharge of 0.022% accrues on unpaid national and local taxes. Failure to prepare or submit transfer-pricing documentation may cause the tax authority to compute income without the taxpayer's contemporaneous comparability evidence and invite penalties under the Law on Coordination of International Tax Affairs. Fraudulent evasion is prosecuted under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, carrying imprisonment of up to 3 years and fines up to 3 times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate statutory withholding on dividends paid to a non-resident corporate shareholder: 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surtax (10% of the 20% national tax).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced or zero DTA withholding, the non-resident shareholder must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate ('TRC') from its residence jurisdiction, complete the Korean withholding-tax treaty relief application, and provide a beneficial-ownership declaration confirming that it is not a conduit and has full entitlement to the dividend. The application package must be delivered to the Korean withholding payer before the dividend payment; the Korean payer then applies the treaty rate if the conditions are satisfied; the National Tax Service may later demand CIGA evidence, financial substance, employee presence, and business rationale. Retroactive relief without prior application is generally unavailable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates on outbound interest and royalties are 20% national withholding plus 2% local income tax surtax, aggregating 22%. Under applicable DTAs, interest rates are commonly reduced to 0%-15% depending on lender and recipient type, and royalty rates commonly to 0%-15% depending on IP category; treaty relief always requires prior TRC, beneficial-ownership declaration, and compliance with Limitation-on-Benefits or Principal-Purpose tests.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 10,000,000,000 in cross-border related-party transactions for a Local File; KRW 100,000,000,000 for a combined Master File and Local File, as provided under Article 11 of the Law on Coordination of International Tax Affairs and its Enforcement Decree.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea is not an ESR offshore zero-tax jurisdiction, but the Economic Substance Regulations framework and Core Income-Generating Activities analysis are central to treaty benefit entitlement and transfer pricing. The Korean IVD manufacturing LLC must demonstrate physical facilities, manufacturing employees, technical oversight, inventory risk, regulatory compliance under the Medical Devices Act, real decision-making, and actual cash flows. A foreign owner's nominal corporate existence in a tax treaty jurisdiction without substantive CIGA in that jurisdiction will be disregarded for DTA purposes, and substance in Korea under the place-of-effective-management test determines domestic taxation of the LLC.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion Through Shell Manufacturing and Artificial Loss Allocation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC sells its IVD products to a foreign related distributor at cost or below cost, maintains no meaningful Korean employees, manufacturing capacity, or operational substance, and shifts all profit offshore while the Korean entity records continuous losses and receives no arm's-length compensation for its R&D and manufacturing functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3(1) of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act imposes imprisonment of up to 3 years or a fine of up to 3 times the tax evaded. Corporate Tax Act Article 67 allows income reallocation in the form of dividends, wages, bonuses, or other outflows to the controlling non-resident, and the Framework Act on National Taxes imposes 40% dishonest-underreporting penalty plus daily overdue interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Korean courts pierce the corporate veil where the LLC is a sham used to evade tax; the director can be personally liable for the corporation's unpaid tax and damages under Commercial Act Article 401. The National Tax Service may impose a departure restriction (travel ban) on the responsible director, seize personal bank accounts and real estate, and recommend criminal indictment resulting in imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance and Failure to Maintain Contemporaneous Documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The taxpayer fails to prepare and submit the Master File or Local File despite foreign related-party transactions above the statutory KRW 10 billion or KRW 100 billion thresholds, fails to perform a benchmark search, maintains no functional and risk analysis, and signs intercompany contracts for management fees, royalties, and loan interest that have no economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 4 and 11 of the Law on Coordination of International Tax Affairs, the tax authority may determine a deemed arm's-length profit and make a unilateral adjustment; if the undisclosed related-party transaction is detected, the taxpayer faces 10%-40% understatement penalties, daily delinquency surcharges, and possible additional 20% penalty for failure to submit required related-party schedules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false transfer-pricing declarations may be held jointly liable under the corporate veil-piercing doctrine and Commercial Act Article 401 for the resulting tax and creditor damage. The responsible officer can be blacklisted and prohibited from departing Korea, personal assets can be attached for restitution, and persistent false documentation is referred for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Criminal Act anti-forgery provisions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Shopping and DTA Relief Abuse Through Beneficial-Ownership Conduits
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean LLC channels dividends, interest, or royalty payments to an intermediary corporation located in a low-tax treaty jurisdiction that has no office, no employees, no economic risk, no CIGA, and no real entitlement, and the conduit immediately back-to-backs the payment to the ultimate non-resident parent to capture an improperly reduced withholding tax rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Korea denies treaty benefits under the general anti-abuse rule and tax treaty principal-purpose provisions; the intermediary is disregarded and the statutory 22% WHT is recovered from the Korean payer, together with 10%-40% underreporting penalties, daily interest, and the disallowance of any deduction for interest or royalties that were not beneficially entitled.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who structure or approve the conduit arrangement are personally exposed to civil restitution for the unpaid withheld taxes and may be jointly liable under the corporate veil-piercing doctrine. In egregious cases, the National Tax Service requests a departure ban (travel blacklisting), assets of the director are frozen and seized, and criminal charges under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and the Act on Special Cases concerning Establishment of Deep-Sea Fisheries? are replaced by the general tax-evasion articles, leading to imprisonment of up to 5 years when multiple years of sophisticated treaty abuse are proven.
